title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The ‘Le Chéile: Together for an inclusive better world project in Central and West Africa, implemented by Sightsavers Ireland, aims to strengthen, and integrate climate action across inclusive education activities. Social unrest in some regions in Cameroon along with climate related disaster, has resulted in internal displacement. Displacement can have a significant and traumatic impact on children, especially children with disabilities, on their wellbeing, education, and childhood. Sightsavers will advocate with the regional delegations of the Ministry of Basic Education and selected inclusive schools to identify children affected by trauma due to climate disaster induced displacement and provide support to ensure their enrolment, retention, and wellbeing in schools.The project will identify a training module for teachers and inclusion champions on psycho-social support for children affected by climate disaster displacement. Children with and without disabilities, identified with trauma will be referred for further psychosocial support by teachers and inclusion champions.Basic training of teachers and inclusion champions in selected schools on climate will help sensitize and promote awareness on climate change. The project will also support children with disabilities’ participation in existing child-to-child clubs, school councils and school civic clubs, with discussions and debates on climate change and action.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: Increased integration of climate action initiatives, especially on climate adaptation, into inclusive education work in Cameroon . SPECIFIC OUTCOME: Adaptation:- The project will respond specifically to children affected by climate related displacement in participating inclusive schools to support their learning, development and provide referral for psychosocial support.- Training of inclusion champions, teachers and social workers on climate change and how to take care of those children will increase awareness on climate related impacts and how to support children impacted by climate related trauma.
